(From the judgment and order dated 2-11-2009, passed by this Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos.1441-1442 of 2009.)

(From the judgment and decree dated 8-4-1985, passed by the High Court Division in civil Revision No. 15 of 1984)
full_judgment:
Mirza Hussain Haider J: Both these civil appeals, by leave, are directed against the judgment and order dated 2-11-2009, passed by this Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos. 1441-1442 of 2009 dismissing the same and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 9-4-2009, passed by the High Court Division in First Appeals No.439 of 2003 and 142 of 2004 affirming the judgement and decree dated 30-10-2003, passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Bogra, in Other Class Suit No.97 of 1997 decreeing the suit.

2. Facts leading to filing of these two civil appeals, in short, are:

That the respondent No.1, as plaintiff, instituted Other Class Suit No. 97 of 1997 for declaration of title and mandatory injunction in respect of 3500 Ajutangsha of land (as described in the schedule of the plaint) in CS Plot No. 1219 RS Plot No. 3818 appertaining to CS Khatian No. 588, MRR Khatian No. 829, RS Khatian (attested) No.3860 of Sutrapur Mouza within Bogra Pourashava, District-Bogra, contending intern alia that the suit land originally belonged to Md Haider Ali Khan Panni who possessed the same by constructing building and planting various type of frees. On the death of the said Md Haider Ali Khan Panni his two sons, namely, Mohammad Ali Khan Panni @ Sayeed Ali Khan Panni and Mehedi Ali Khan Panni have been possessing the same as their guest house. Sayeed Ali Khan Panni, who was in possession of the suit land died leaving behind proforma defendants No. 5 to 9 as his legal heirs, who while jointly possessing the same for over 12 years, made some renovations in the suit land including erecting boundary walls and planting trees of various types. Subsequently, they transferred the suit land by two registered deeds No. 14492 and 14493 both dated 31-8-1997 to the plaintiff and handed over the possession thereof. It is alleged that inspite of the fact that the Government has no right, title and interest in the suit land had been trying to Dispossess the plaintiff from the same, Hence the suit.

3. Defendants No. 1, 2 and 4 contested the suit, by filing written statement, denying all the materials allegation and contending inter alia that the suit land along with other lands was requisitioned in 1957 for Agricultural Extension Department in accordance with law and possession was handed over to the requiring body on 8-5-1958. Since then the same is being used by the aforesaid defendants for more than 12 years. In the meantime, the Government having decided to acquire the property finally and took all steps in accordance with law and by final publication of the same in the Gazette Notification publishing on 4th May, 1961 0.62 acre of land in CS Plots No. 1210, 1216 and 1219 were finally acquired the Agricultural Department after taking possession of the said acquired land including the suit plot (CS Plot No. 1219), constructed several structures on the same upon obtaining permission from the Bogra Paurashava. The defendants paid tax, electric and telephone bills to the respective authority by opening separate khatian No. 4671 in the name of defendant No. 2 lawfully. Thus the plaintiff or the proforma defendant who were stated by heirs of Haider Ali Khan Panni have no right, title and interest in the suit land. The alleged- deeds of the plaintiff are forged, fabricated and manufactured by which no title and possession vested upon the plaintiff.

4. The suit was decreed by the learned Joint District Judge, Court No.1, Bogra by the judgment and decree dated 30-10-2003 against which the defendants No. 2 and 1 preferred First Appeal No. 439 of 2003 and First Appeal No. 142 of 2004 before the High Court Division.

5. A Division Bench of the High Court Division, heard both the appeals together and ultimately dismissed the same by judgment and decree dated 9-4-2009 affirming those of the trial Court. As against the same the present appellants filed Civil Petitions for Leave to Appeal No.1441-1442 of 2009 before this Division which have been dismissed by judgment and order dated 2-11-2009.

6. Hence, the defendant-appellants filed two Civil Review Petitions No.101 and 102 of 2010 and obtained leave which gave rise to these two Appeals.

7. On the other hand the Government filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 354 of 2017 against the judgment and decree dated 8-4-1985, passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 15 of 1984 discharging the Rule and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 7-8-1983 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Bogra, in Other Class Appeal No. 6 of 1983 reversing the judgment and decree dated 31-5-1982 passed by the then Munsif, 2nd Court, Sadar, Bogra, decreeing Other Suit No. 42 of 1979 filed by Romani Madhab Das in respect of Plot No. 1210 as stated before.

8. In the said suit Romani Madhab Das (Respondent No.1) prayed for a declaration that the notice of ejectment dated 8-1-1979 issued by the then Sub- Divisional Officer (SDO) Sadar, Bogra, is illegal, null and void, ultra vices, malafide, without jurisdiction and not binding upon the: plaintiff with a prayer for permanent and mandatory injunction in respect of suit land in Plot No. 1210 within Sutrapur Thana, Bogra, contending that he inherited the suit land from his father, late Gour Hari Das and got his name recorded in MRR Khatian (CS Khatian) No. 589; Earlier by filing Other Class Suit No. 226 of 1975 he obtained a decree of permanent injunction against the government in respect of suit Plot No. 1210. Inspite of the said decree the SDO Bogra, issued notice dated 8-1-1979 alleging that the plaintiff is illegally possessing some portion of land of Agricultural Seed Godown at Lalmonirhat (Part of Suit land), he was compelled to file the instant suit to protect his house over the suit land. He never encroached upon any land covered by the said notice and the defendants most illegally made some constructions over a part of the suit land.

9. Defendant No. 2 (petitioner No. 1 herein) contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the allegations and thereby contending inter alia that the suit is not maintainable, the same is barred by limitation as well as in law; The defendant contended that the suit land along with other lands (CS Plot No. 1210, 1216 and 1219) were requisitioned in 1957-58 and subsequently finally acquired by the government for public purpose vide notification No. Beg.No.11/Br. 22/58/296 dated 22-4-1961 and published in the gazette dated 4-5-1961; who the plaintiff is a trespasser who encroached into the said government land and as such the notice in question was legally served upon him for vacating the suit land. It is further stated that in the said suit he also prayed for temporary injunction against which the plaintiff unsuccessfully preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 49 of 1979. The government constructed Seed Godown on the aforesaid plots and erected boundary walls. It is alleged that during the period of holidays from 3-9-1978 to 6-9-1978 the plaintiff constructed a but on a portion of the suit plot and as such the government issued the notice upon the plaintiff for vacating the government land and, as such, there is no illegality in issuing the notice and the suit challenging the said notice in question on finally acquired Land is liable to be dismissed.

10. On hearing the said suit was decreed by judgment and decree dated 31-5-1982 against which the government (defendant) unsuccessfully preferred Other Class Appeal No. 6 of 1983. Against the said judgment and decree dated 7-8-1983 passed in Other Class Appeal No. 6 of 1983 the government moved the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 15 of 1984 and obtained Rule which was ultimately discharged by the impugned judgment and decree dated 8-4-1985. Hence this civil petition for leave to appeal.

11. Mr Mahabuby Alam, the learned Attorney General, appearing on behalf of the appellants as well as for the petitioner submits that the suit land has been finally acquired which has been notified in the gazette date 4th may, 1961 and these being legal bar in challenging such acquisition in suits; the trial Court as well as the High Court Division committed error of law in decreeing the suit. He submits that the said factual and legal position also has not been considered by this Division while dismissing the leave petitions. Thus the said judgment of this Division is required to be reviewed. He further submits that earlier in Title Suit No. 148 of 1965, instituted by Mehadi Ali Khan Panni, alleged predecessor of the plaintiff, prayed for his tittle in Plot No.1216 and obtained decree and in another suit being Title Suit No. 42 of 1979 filed by one Ramoni Madhab Das, notice dated 8th January, 1979 for eviction of the occupants of Plot No. 1210 has been declared illegal. But since plot Nos. 1210, 1216 and 1219 are maintainable under section 14A of the Specific Relief Act and, as such, dismissal of the leave petitions, which relates to Plot No. 1219, is required to be reviewed and, as such, the instant appeals should be allowed. He next submits that this Division, while affirming the decree of mandatory injunction, did not consider that there is no allegation made in the plaint that the government made construction on the suit land during the pendency of the instant suit, which is an error apparent on the face of the record. Hence dismissal of the leave petition is thus erroneous and the judgment complained of herein is required to be reviewed. He finally submits that admittedly the plaintiff of the instant suit is not in possession of the suit plot and he having not prayed for recovery of possession, as consequential relief, decreeing the suit upto this Division is erroneous and, as such, the judgment passed by this Division is required to be reviewed and thereby both the appeals should be allowed.

12. Mr Sharifuddin Chaklader, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of plaintiff-respondent No.1 submits that the Government has miserably failed to prove by producing any evidence that the suit land was ever acquired nor they could prove; that any prior or subsequent notice for requisition and acquisition, in prescribed form, was ever served upon the plaintiff. They even failed to produce any material to show that there was proposal of the Deputy Commissioner for requisition or acquisition of the suit land or initiation of any LA case or payment of compensation etc. Therefore, he submits that the alleged bar to file a suit on the plea of requisition or acquisition does not arise at all. He next submits that the trial Court as well as the High Court Division concurrently found that the suit of the plaintiff-respondent No. 1 is competent and maintain-able under sections 42 and 55 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree calls for no interference by this Division. He next submits that there is no overriding public purpose/interest or national/public interest to defeat the lawful right, title, interest and possession of the plaintiff-respondent No.1, which has been accrued by dint of two duly registered sale deeds in 1997. He finally submits that the appellants are under a legal obligation to remove the illegally constructed structures from the suit land and, as such, there is no merit in the appeals and therefore, the same are liable to be dismissed.

13. Having considered the submissions of the learned Advocates of both the sides and on perusal of the judgment under review and other materials on record it appears that the appellant/petitioner claim that the three plots being CS Plot Nos. 1210, 1216 and 1219 subject matter of three suits have been acquired by the government which have been published in the gazette notification dated 4-5-1961. Thus the points to be determined are whether (i) on the face of section 5(7) read with section 14A of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 a suit, in respect of an acquired properly, is maintainable; (ii) Plot No. 1210 being not the subject matter of earlier Title Suits, wherein the title of the plaintiffs of those suits have been declared along with injunction, decreeing those suits subject matter of which are finally acquired by the government, decreeing the suits and dismissal of the civil petitions are erroneous; (iii) in the absence of any construction being made by the appellants in the suit land during the pendency of the suit granting of mandatory injunction is justified; and (iv) whether in the absence of seeking consequential relief by way of recovery of possession the present suit is maintainable under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act .

14. The appellants claim that the suit land was requisitioned in the year 1957 for setting up the office of the Thana Agricultural Officer, Bogra and after compliance of all legal formalities the same was finally acquired by publishing in the gazette on 4-5-1961 under section 5(7) of the Act of 1948. Since then the defendants No.2 to 4 are possessing the same which has been correctly recorded in the Khatian in the name of Agricultural Extension Office.

<u>15. Section 5(7) of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act 1948 provides that after requisition on completion of all formalities in section 5(1) to 5(6) the Government shall then publish in the Official Gazette a notice to the effect that the Government has decided to acquire the requisitioned property. On and from the beginning of the day on which the notice is so published the requisitioned property shall vest absolutely in the Government free from all encumbrances and the period of such requisition of such property shall end. Thus with the publication of such notice in the gazette under section 5(7) the requisition period shall end and the said land, shall vest absolutely in the government free from all encumbrances. From the Gazette dated 4-5-1961 it appears that CS Plot Nos. 1210, 1216 and 1219 the suit plots of all the three above-mentioned suits have been finally acquired. From the record of Other Class Suit No. 42 of 1979 (CP No. 354 of 2017) it appears that the said Gazette dated 22-4-1961 has been proved and marked as Exhibit-A(i). The fact of such final acquisition of all the three aforesaid plots also appears to have been found by the trial Court in its judgment passed in Other Class Suit No. 97 of 1997. The trial Courts though found the suit lands were finally acquired by Gazette notification under section 5(7) of the Act, but decreed the suits on completely erroneous basis without considering the legal bar as spelt out in section 14A of the Act of 1948. When section 14A of the said Act, 1948 clearly provides 'Except as expressly provided in this Act, no Civil Court shall entertain any suit or application against any order passed or any action taken under this Act and all suits and appeals pending in any such Court against any order passed or any action taken under this Act shall abate with effect from the date of coming into force of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property (Amendment) Ordinance, 1963; it imposes an express bar on entertainment of any suit or appeal against any order passed or action taken under the Act.</u>

<u>16. Apart from the above, the learned Attorney General filed an Additional Paper Book annexing a copy of the Gazette dated 4-5-1961 for perusal and consideration of this Division. On perusal of which it appears that the said three suit plots containing 0.62 acre of land in total have been acquired upon complying with all formalities of law and the final acquisition has been published in the said gazette under section 5(7) of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 which has been notified through the official gazette and, as such, it has the force of law. Under Article 152 of the Constitution "law" means any Act, Ordinance, Order, rule, regulation, bye-law, notification or other legal instrument, and any custom or usage, having the force of law in Bangladesh. Gazette being the notification under the aforesaid Article of the Constitution has the force of law. Thus the acquisition being finally published in the gazette it has the force of law and, as such, challenging any action taken by the government pursuant to (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 is totally barred under section 14A of the said Act.</u>

17. Here in these cases, when the suit lands have been acquired finally by the Government for the extension of the Agricultural office in 1961 by publishing in the gazette as per law and since then the same has been vested in the government free from all encumbrances suits filed in 1965 or in 1979 or in 1997 are not at all maintainable and any decree passed in those suits are also completely nullity in the eye of law no matter whether the same have been affirmed in higher courts. When the basis of a decree/order is void/ any consequence thereof is also void. Thus once a property is finally acquired by gazette notification published under section 5(7) of the Act of 1948, section 14A of the said Act of 1948 operates as a bar- to file any suit relating to the property finally acquired. As such we are of the view that pursuant to the above provision of law, since the Court, had no jurisdiction to entertain any action taken or order passed under the said Act, the judgment and decree obtained in those suits and affirmed by the higher courts are completely erroneous, void and without lawful authority.

18. Since the lands in question have been, acquired and since there is an express bar in law to challenge such acquisition in any suit before any civil Court and since the same has been addressed above, other questions are not required to be addressed.

<u>19. From the above scenario a pertinent question may arise as to whether compensation have been paid to the affected persons whose lands have been acquired by the government. Article 42 of the Constitution provides 'every citizen shall have the right to acquire, hold, transfer or otherwise dispose of property and no property of a citizen shall be compulsorily acquired, nationalised or requisitioned save by the authority of law on payment of appropriate compensation. Payment of adequate/appropriate compensation in lieu of acquisition is a constitutional right of a citizen. Non payment of such compensation shall fully frustrate/ affect the constitutional right of the affected person. From the records it appears that the defendant-appellants failed to prove that against the requisition/acquisition of the suit plots any/adequate compensation has been paid to the affected person.</u>

20. In the present cases question may arise who are the affected persons and who can claim or be paid compensation pursuant to such acquisition of the lands described in the gazette notification dated 4-5-1961. By filing additional paper book dated 7-2-2017 the appellant (government) stated that suit plot no. 1219 was the land of the Waqf Estate from whom the same has been requisitioned first and then acquired by the government and the same has been notified in the gazette on 4-5-1961. But on perusal of the judgment of the trial Court dated 30-11-2003 passed in Other Class Suit No. 97 of 1997 it appears that the suit plots belonged to Zaminder Haider Ali Khan Panni of Korotia. But, Exhibit-'Ka' dated 17-2-1955, upon which, the defendant relied to claim that the suit plots are waqf property 'is not a deed of waqf and it does not contain any description of any property. Such paper has no relevancy about the ownership/title of any property. Considering all these aspects both the courts below held that 'the plaintiff respondent herein has lawful right, title and interest in the suit property'. So the claim of the government-appellant that 'admittedly the property was the land of an Waqf Estate' is not at all sustainable. Since none, but the subsequent purchasers/ transferees' of the original owner have come and instituted the suit claiming their title in the suit plots, they should not be deprived of adequate compensation. Hence we are of the view that the plaintiff-respondents are entitled to receive the compensation of the land which have been acquired by the government as a matter of their constitutional right.

21. All these aspects having not been considered, by this Division while dismissing the civil petitions earlier by the judgment under review, we find substance in these appeals as well as in the civil petition for leave to appeal No. 354 of 2017. Hence the findings and decision arrived at by the High Court Division under the aforesaid facts and circumstances being not based on proper appreciation of fact and law are required to be interfered with by this Division. Accordingly, the judgment and orders of the High Court Division are set aside. Consequently the judgment and order under review is also set aside.

22. The appellants are directed to assess and pay adequate compensation, if not paid earlier, to the respondents, who are affected persons, in accordance with law.

Accordingly, both the civil appeals are allowed with the above observations and direction. However, without any order as to cost. The leave petition No. 354 of 2017 is disposed of, upon condoning the delay caused in filing the same, in the light of the above judgment.

End.
